goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — Feed-supplied HTML is persisted with the raw_html cook method, so an untrusted feed entry can store executable markup and XSS every topic viewer.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in app/models/topic_embed.rb line 22, PostCreator is called with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which according to app/models/post.rb lines 131-133 means `return raw` - the raw HTML is stored directly without sanitization. The content comes from external RSS/ATOM feeds (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) or remote URLs (import_remote method). The only processing is CGI.unescapeHTML and absolutize_urls, neither of which sanitize for XSS. This allows untrusted feed content containing malicious scripts to be stored and rendered to users, creating a stored XSS vulnerability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — The host check applies only before open-uri follows redirects, allowing a page on the allowed host to redirect the server-side fetch to internal addresses.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, in app/models/topic_embed.rb line 48, the import_remote method uses `open(url).read` to fetch content from a URL. The embeddable_host check happens in topic_retriever.rb's invalid_host? method which checks `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host` - this only validates the initial URL's host. However, open-uri (Ruby's open() for URLs) follows HTTP redirects by default. If an attacker controls a page on the allowed embeddable_host, they could set up a redirect to internal addresses (like 127.0.0.1, internal services, cloud metadata endpoints, etc.), and the server would follow that redirect and fetch the internal resource. This is a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability. The finding correctly identifies that the host validation occurs before redirects are followed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — A crash or Redis error between SETNX and EXPIRE leaves a non-expiring throttle key that silently blocks all future retrievals for that URL.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 25-30 that SETNX and EXPIRE are called as separate operations. If a crash, Redis error, or process termination occurs between the SETNX (line 26) and EXPIRE (line 27), the key will be set without an expiration. This would permanently block future retrievals for that URL since the key would never expire. This is a real race condition/atomicity bug in the code introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:12 — With retries disabled and no per-item error isolation, one malformed feed item aborts the whole poll and prevents every later item from importing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows poll_feed.rb with `sidekiq_options retry: false` at line 12, and the `poll_feed` method iterates through `rss.items.each` without any try/catch around individual item processing. If any item causes an exception (e.g., malformed content, missing fields like `i.content` being nil when calling `.scrub`), the entire job fails and subsequent items are not processed. With retries disabled, this means those items are permanently skipped until the next hourly poll. This is a real correctness issue - one bad feed item prevents processing of all subsequent items.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:10 — Passing the full Referer URL as postMessage targetOrigin does not match the parent origin when it contains a path, so resize messages are silently discarded.
matched_golden_ids: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments identify the same issue: using the full Referer URL instead of just the origin (scheme+host+port) as the postMessage targetOrigin will cause the resize messages to fail/be dropped. The golden comment explains it should be 'origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL' and the candidate says 'full Referer URL as postMessage targetOrigin does not match the parent origin when it contains a path'. Both point to the same bug with the same consequence (messages being dropped/discarded, preventing resizing).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — Passing the full Referer URL as postMessage targetOrigin rejects normal embedding pages with a path, so the public resize protocol never reaches its caller.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that passing the full Referer URL as postMessage targetOrigin will reject normal embedding pages with a path. Looking at the diff, in app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb line 11, the code uses `request.referer` as the targetOrigin. The postMessage API's targetOrigin parameter checks the origin (scheme + host + port), not the full URL path. When a full URL is passed, the browser extracts just the origin portion for comparison. So passing 'http://example.com/some/path' as targetOrigin will still match messages to 'http://example.com'. The finding misunderstands how postMessage targetOrigin works - it doesn't require an exact URL match, just origin match.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:28 — A worker crash after SETNX but before EXPIRE leaves the throttle key permanent, so that embed URL can remain stuck loading forever.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 24-30 that SETNX is called followed by EXPIRE on the next line. If the process crashes or is killed between these two Redis operations, the key will be set without an expiration, causing it to persist indefinitely. This would permanently block retrieval for that embed URL since retrieved_recently? would always return true. This is a real race condition bug in the code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 — Relative href/src values without a leading slash are not made absolute, so imported article links and images resolve against the embed iframe rather than their source page.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the absolutize_urls method in app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 56-73, the code only handles URLs that start with '/': `if href.present? && href.start_with?('/')`. Relative URLs without a leading slash (e.g., 'images/photo.jpg' or 'page.html') would not be matched by this condition and would remain relative. When the content is displayed in an embed iframe on a different domain, these relative URLs would resolve against the iframe's URL rather than the original source page, causing broken links and images. This is a real bug in the URL absolutization logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — force: true` drops any existing `topic_embeds` table and its data before recreating it

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb, the migration uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`. However, this is a NEW migration file being created (indicated by the 'new file mode' in the diff header). For a new migration that creates a new table, using `force: true` is not a bug - it's a common pattern to ensure the migration can be re-run cleanly during development. The table didn't exist before this migration, so there's no data loss risk. Additionally, in production, migrations run sequentially and only once, so `force: true` wouldn't cause issues there either.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — force: true` drops any existing `top_topics` table and its data before recreating it

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the migration file db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb was modified to add 'force: true' to create_table. This option drops any existing table with that name before creating a new one, which could cause data loss if the migration is run on a database that already has a top_topics table with data. The diff clearly shows the change from 'create_table :top_topics do |t|' to 'create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|'.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20 — feed_key and its Digest dependency are unused dead code, leaving an implied caching contract with no implementation.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that `feed_key` method (lines 20-22) is defined but never called anywhere in the diff. The method creates a Redis key using Digest::SHA1 but is not used in `poll_feed` or anywhere else. This appears to be dead code that was likely intended for caching/throttling but was never implemented. While not a bug (the code works without it), it's a legitimate code quality concern about unused code that implies incomplete functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:46 — Reads and parses an entire remote page without a byte limit, so a large embeddable document can exhaust a worker's memory.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 44-48, the import_remote method calls `open(url).read` without any byte limit, then passes the entire content to Readability::Document. The diff shows: `doc = Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, tags: %w[div p code pre h1 h2 h3 b em i strong a img], attributes: %w[href src])`. This is a real security/availability concern - a malicious or very large embeddable document could exhaust worker memory since there's no size limit on the HTTP response being read into memory.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:28 — Iterates and imports every feed item without a limit or incremental cursor, so a large feed causes unbounded work on every hourly poll.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that poll_feed.rb lines 27-33 iterate over all rss.items without any limit or pagination. The code does `rss.items.each do |i|` and calls TopicEmbed.import for each item. While TopicEmbed.import does check if an embed already exists (avoiding duplicate creation), the iteration itself processes every item in the feed on every hourly poll. For large feeds, this could cause significant work. However, this is more of a performance/scalability concern than a bug - the code will function correctly, just potentially inefficiently. The finding is grounded in actual diff code and represents a legitimate architectural concern for the new feature.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — The scheduled job fetches the configured feed without open or read timeouts, so a hung upstream can indefinitely occupy a worker.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb line 29, the code uses `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` from the 'open-uri' library without specifying any timeout options. The open-uri library by default has no read timeout, meaning if the upstream server hangs or is slow to respond, the worker thread will block indefinitely. This is a real defect in a scheduled job that runs hourly - a hung upstream could occupy a Sidekiq worker indefinitely, potentially causing resource exhaustion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — Remote article retrieval has no open or read timeout, allowing a nonresponsive embed host to indefinitely block a background job.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at app/models/topic_embed.rb line 48, the code uses `open(url).read` without any timeout configuration. The `open` method from 'open-uri' (which is required via ruby-readability) will block indefinitely if the remote server doesn't respond. This is called from a background job (Jobs::RetrieveTopic), and an unresponsive host could block the worker indefinitely. This is a real defect - network operations should have timeouts to prevent resource exhaustion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — SETNX and EXPIRE are separate operations, so an interruption between them leaves a non-expiring throttle key that prevents all future retrievals for that URL.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a race condition in lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 26-29. The code uses SETNX followed by a separate EXPIRE call. If the process crashes or is interrupted between these two operations, the key will exist without an expiration, permanently blocking future retrievals for that URL. This is a real bug - the atomic alternative would be to use SET with EX/NX options (SET key value EX 60 NX) or use a Lua script. The diff clearly shows this pattern at lines 26-29 of the new file.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — Defaulting `cook_method` to `raw_html` makes every newly created post bypass HTML sanitization, enabling stored XSS for ordinary users.

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the code. Looking at the migration in db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb, it sets default: 1. Looking at app/models/post.rb, the cook_methods enum is defined as Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html), which means :regular is 0 and :raw_html is 1. However, the default of 1 means raw_html, but examining the cook method in post.rb shows it only bypasses cooking when cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]. The default being 1 (raw_html) would indeed be concerning, but looking at the Enum implementation pattern in Rails/Discourse, Enum.new typically starts at 1 for the first value, not 0. So :regular would be 1 and :raw_html would be 2. The default of 1 corresponds to :regular, not :raw_html. This means normal posts still go through the regular cooking/sanitization pipeline.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — Imported RSS content is persisted and rendered as raw HTML without sanitization, so malicious feed content can execute script in the forum origin.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in app/models/topic_embed.rb line 22, PostCreator is called with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. Looking at app/models/post.rb lines 131-133, when cook_method is :raw_html, the cook method returns `raw` directly without any processing. The RSS content from external feeds (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb line 33: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) is passed through TopicEmbed.import and stored as raw HTML. While CGI.unescapeHTML decodes HTML entities, it does not sanitize malicious content. The content is then rendered via `raw post.cooked` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb line 17, which outputs unescaped HTML. This creates an XSS vulnerability where malicious feed content containing script tags would execute in the forum's origin.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:43 — The new controller test expects a direct TopicRetriever call even though the action enqueues :retrieve_topic, so the test fails instead of verifying the delivered job.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the embed_controller.rb shows that when no topic_id is found, it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` (line 14-15). However, the test at spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:41-46 sets up expectations like `TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`, expecting a direct TopicRetriever call. But the controller actually enqueues a job, not calling TopicRetriever directly. The TopicRetriever is called inside the job (lib/topic_retriever.rb), not in the controller. This means the test's expectations are incorrect - it expects direct TopicRetriever instantiation when the controller actually enqueues a job. The test would fail because TopicRetriever.new is never called directly by the controller.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:32 — The retriever specs mock both private control-flow methods, leaving Redis throttling, feed fallback, and HTTP import behavior untested.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test at spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb mocks `perform_retrieve` and `retrieved_recently?` which are private methods. Looking at the diff, the actual implementation in lib/topic_retriever.rb includes Redis throttling logic in `retrieved_recently?`, feed polling fallback in `perform_retrieve`, and HTTP import via `fetch_http`. The tests only verify that `perform_retrieve` is called or not called based on host validation and throttle checks, but they mock these methods rather than testing their actual behavior. This is a legitimate test coverage concern for newly added nontrivial logic - the Redis throttling, feed fallback, and HTTP import paths are not exercised by these tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:31 — PollFeed tests only mock delegation and never cover parsing a feed or importing its HTTP/ID URL variants.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb only tests the execute method's delegation logic (checking that poll_feed is called when settings are configured), but doesn't test the actual poll_feed method which contains significant logic: parsing RSS feeds with SimpleRSS, handling URL variants (using i.link or i.id), unescaping HTML content, and calling TopicEmbed.import. This is newly added nontrivial logic in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb that lacks test coverage for its core functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — The new skip_validations persistence path has no regression test proving invalid revisions are saved only when requested.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a change in lib/post_revisor.rb at line 85 where `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` is introduced, allowing posts to be saved without validation when skip_validations is passed. Looking at the test files added (spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb), there are tests for TopicEmbed.import which uses skip_validations, but there's no direct test in the diff for the PostRevisor's skip_validations behavior specifically. The finding correctly identifies that this new code path for skipping validations during revision lacks a dedicated regression test. This is a legitimate test coverage concern for newly added functionality.
